Entry requirements · 2027 entry

Computer Science BS at University of Southern California

What University of Southern California asks of applicants to Computer Science BS for 2027 entry (the 2026–27 application cycle). Each requirement below is labelled verified, partly verified or not verified, with the date it was checked and a link to the official source.

US · All University of Southern California courses · Computer Science field guide

Entry requirements 2027 entry 5 of 8 verified
SAT / ACT
  • Test-optional for first-year applicants for the 2027–28 academic year — SAT/ACT not required
  • If submitted, scores must be official (sent by the testing agency); self-reported scores are not accepted
Verified19 Oct 2026USC: International Students · USC: First-Year Students
English language
  • USC-approved English exam required for all international applicants whose native language is not English — no waivers
  • Recommended minimums:
    • TOEFL iBT 100 (each section 20+) before 21 Jan 2026, or 5 (each section 4+) from 21 Jan 2026
    • IELTS 7
    • C1 Advanced 185 (each skill 169+)
    • PTE 68
    • SAT EBRW 650
    • ACT English 27
  • Duolingo English Test only if unable to sit an approved exam: minimum 130 (admitted students with only Duolingo must take USC’s International Student Exam on arrival)

USC calls these “recommended minimums” and says applicants are admissible below them at reduced rates of admission. USC also publishes an admitted-student TOEFL average (above 111), which is not a requirement and is not shown.

Verified19 Oct 2026USC: International Students
Admissions tests

None listed on the official source

Verified19 Oct 2026USC: First-Year Students
Subject prerequisites
  • Not used in Altiora’s matching yet — see the note for the official guidance

Official: C or better in at least three years of high-school mathematics, including Algebra II (all USC applicants). USC Viterbi adds that at least one year of Calculus is important preparation for all engineering or computer science majors (preparation advice, not stated as a requirement).

Partly verified19 Oct 2026USC: What We Look For · USC Viterbi: Apply (First-Year)
A-Level requirements
Grades
Not recorded
Details
I/GCSE results plus predicted results for all A-Level subjects (and EPQ, if applicable) must be provided; students are admitted on predicted A-Levels and verify final results later. I/GCSE results alone are not sufficient. No A-Level subject requirements for entry.

USC states that competitive applicants have predicted B or above in at least three A-Levels — a description of competitive applicants, not a minimum offer, so no grades are shown as a requirement.

Verified19 Oct 2026USC: Academic Expectations for International Students
IB requirements
Overall score
Not recorded
Details
USC typically expects the full IB Diploma Programme; predicted grades should be included with the transcript.

Official: “We typically expect the full IB Diploma Programme, with strong academic performance (scores of 5-7 on all HL and SL exams) across all subjects.”

Partly verified19 Oct 2026USC: Academic Expectations for International Students
Other qualifications
  • Home-schooled applicants: USC recommends submitting externally graded work such as AP exam results, if possible

USC’s admissions pages checked (First-Year Students, International Students, Test Optional FAQ, What We Look For) do not say how AP scores are treated for other applicants; the recommendation above is stated only for home-schooled applicants.

Partly verified19 Oct 2026USC: Test Optional FAQ
Other requirements
  • No additional Viterbi application, test scores or materials — apply to USC and list a Viterbi (VSE) major as first choice
  • USC short answers plus the Common App essay
  • No admission interviews by the Office of Undergraduate Admission
Verified19 Oct 2026USC Viterbi: Apply (First-Year) · USC: What We Look For · USC: First-Year Students
